text: Once a year the Sun enters your 1st house, and for roughly a month the light falls on you rather than on your obligations. This is the start of your personal year in a real sense. Energy tends to rise. You feel more like yourself, more visible, more willing to take up room. People notice you again, and you notice yourself: how you look, what you want, whether the life you are living still fits the person living it. The early days of the pass can feel like waking up, especially if the weeks before were foggy or tired. Use them to surface. The middle of the transit is the peak. Initiative comes easiest then, asking for what you want feels natural instead of forced, and a first impression lands with more force than usual. A project begun in these weeks stays yours in a way later starts do not, so this is a good window for anything that needs your name and your face on it: the introduction, the launch, the honest conversation about what you need. The risks are mild but real. With the light on you, self-focus can tip into not hearing anyone else, and the urge to act can outrun the plan. You may also feel a flash of impatience with people who still treat you as last year's version of yourself. Let them catch up; you have changed faster than their picture of you. As the Sun approaches the far end of the house, the surge settles into something steadier, and your attention begins drifting toward practical questions, money, resources, what all this renewed energy is actually for. That is the natural close of the season, not a loss. The pass is quick and it returns every year, so nothing has to be crammed into these few weeks. Treat it instead as your annual appointment with yourself. Decide one true thing about who you are now, act on it while the energy is high, and let the rest of the year do the slower work of making it real.

Money and what it buys take the front seat while the Sun moves through your 2nd house. For a few weeks each year, this stretch turns your attention to income, possessions, and the question underneath both: what you value, and whether your resources are serving it. Early in the pass, the theme often arrives as a simple urge to take stock. You look at the accounts, notice what you own, and feel either quietly provisioned or quietly exposed. Either reading is useful information. As the transit peaks, counting sharpens into valuing. You have more clarity than usual about what your time and skill are worth, which makes this a natural window for the raise conversation, the price adjustment, the honest look at whether your work matches what it pays. Confidence about earning tends to run higher now, and effort aimed at income has a way of landing. The appetite side of the house wakes too. You may want to buy things during these weeks, and the pull is usually toward quality: the durable coat, the good tool, the object that makes daily life feel more solid. Enjoying that is part of the point. The watch-out is letting spending do the work that self-respect should be doing. This house ties possessions to esteem, so a thin balance can feel more personal than it is while the light sits here, and a splurge can be a mood wearing a receipt. Nothing about a single month decides your material story. The house also holds values in the wider sense. Somewhere in these weeks you tend to meet a small choice that tests what you actually care about against what merely pays or impresses, and how you choose sets a keel for the year. As the Sun moves on, the money question loosens its grip and your attention scatters back into daily traffic. What lasts from the season is not the purchases but the reckoning: a slightly truer sense of what you have, what you need, and which of your assets cannot be counted. If you do one deliberate thing with the transit, let it be naming, in plain words, the few things you value enough to fund with your time. The year tends to organize itself around whatever you decide here.

Your calendar crowds up when the Sun crosses your 3rd house. Calls multiply, errands stack, short trips appear out of nowhere, and everyone seems to want a reply by Friday. For a few weeks a year, life speeds up at the local level: the neighborhood, the inbox, the daily rounds, the people you see without planning to, siblings and neighbors included. This is not just noise. The light is on your mind, and the season wants you talking, reading, asking, and connecting. Curiosity runs warmer than usual. Subjects you shelved months ago look interesting again, and conversations you have been avoiding start to feel possible, because words come more easily now than they do most of the year. The peak of the pass is a peak of articulation. Whatever needs saying, the pitch, the explanation, the apology, the letter to a brother or sister, tends to come out cleaner in these weeks than before or after them. It is also a strong stretch for learning in short form: the course, the manual, the skill you can pick up in an afternoon and use for a decade. The cost of the season is scatter. Ten open threads can crowd out the one that matters, you can talk straight past your own listening, and it is easy to mistake being busy for being engaged. Commitments made in bulk now have a way of arriving all at once later. As the transit winds down, the pace eases on its own and the pull shifts toward home and quieter ground. Before it does, sort what the weeks brought you. Most of the information passing through will be traffic, and letting it go is fine. But somewhere in the pile there is usually one idea, one conversation, or one small discovery from your own square mile that deserves to outlive the month. Write that one down. The Sun will bring the noise back around next year; what you keep from this pass is the sentence you managed to say clearly while it was here.

Each year the Sun spends a stretch at the bottom of your chart, crossing your 4th house, and the season asks you to come home. Ambition goes quiet for these weeks, or at least turns inward, and the pull runs toward the private side of your life: the household, the family, the past, the rooms where you do not perform. If your energy for public effort dips a little, that is the transit working, not you failing. The light is underground, feeding roots instead of branches. Home tends to ask for attention now, sometimes literally. Repairs, rearranging, a move, a full pantry, guests, or simply the urge to cook and stay in: the house wants you in it, and time spent there repays itself. Family comes forward too. Parents and origins occupy more of your thoughts than usual, and an old family thread, a memory, a grievance, a question about where you come from, often surfaces mid-pass and asks to be handled with adult hands. The peak of this transit is less an event than a settling: a clearer feeling for what your foundation actually needs, which obligations are load-bearing and which are habit. Honor the tiredness if it comes. This is the low tide of your solar year, and resting during it is how the high tide gets funded. The risk is reading the inwardness wrong, either forcing yourself to perform at full daylight brightness and wondering why it costs so much, or sinking into the couch and old wounds and calling it reflection. The season works best with gentle structure: tend one room, have one honest family conversation, revisit one memory on purpose rather than letting them all ambush you. As the Sun climbs out of the house, your appetite for expression and play comes back, usually with interest. What you carry forward is quiet ballast, a household in slightly better order, a past slightly better understood, a base that will hold the louder months coming. Let yourself be unimpressive for these few weeks. The year has other plans for your visibility, and this is where the strength for them gets stored.

Play comes back into season when the Sun lights up your 5th house. For a few weeks each year, the serious machinery of your life loosens and the appetite returns: for making things, for romance, for games, for children and their company, for any hour spent doing something because it delights you. This is the Sun in the part of your chart it cares most about, self-expression, and you can feel the difference. Color returns. You want to be seen enjoying your life, not just running it. Creative work moves well now. Projects that stalled in duller months pick up, and the courage to show what you made, to an audience, a friend, a stranger online, runs higher than usual. Romance warms in the same way. New attractions tend to spark during this pass, and standing relationships benefit from actual courtship: the planned evening, the surprise, the effort of delight. If there are children in your life, they occupy more of the frame now, and time spent playing at their level tends to give back more than it costs. The pass peaks as a kind of shine. You are more expressive, more generous, funnier, and more willing to risk looking foolish, which is the entry fee for most kinds of joy. The shadows are proportionate. Wanting applause can start steering what you make, pride can bruise easily when the response is thin, and drama can substitute for feeling if the weeks get too staged. Appetite can also outrun the budget, since fun bought on impulse is this season's favorite expense. None of it is heavy weather; it just wants noticing. As the Sun moves toward the next house, the party quiets and your attention turns back toward routine and upkeep. Before it does, bank something. Finish the piece, or at least date the draft. Keep one pleasure you rediscovered, a game, a practice, a standing night out, and give it a permanent slot in the ordinary weeks ahead. The transit's real gift is not the month of brightness. It is the reminder, renewed annually, that enjoyment is not a reward for a finished life but part of the fuel that runs one.

The light lands on your workload while the Sun travels through your 6th house. These few weeks are about the unglamorous machinery that keeps your life running: the job's daily tasks, the routines, the body's maintenance, the backlog you have been stepping over for months. Little of it is exciting, and all of it is suddenly visible. That visibility is the gift. Where other seasons blur the daily round, this one shows it to you in sharp focus, and the urge to fix, sort, and improve arrives on its own. Momentum favors order now. Cleaning out the files, restarting the routine, clearing the ten small tasks that have been draining you a little every day: efforts like these move faster than usual and hold better. Work itself tends to intensify during the pass, with more asked of you and more noticed about how you do it. Craft matters this month. Doing the ordinary thing well, on time, without fuss, is the season's version of shining, and colleagues register it even when nobody says so. The body speaks up too. Energy, sleep, food, and strain make themselves felt more plainly than usual, and the pass rewards paying attention to what your daily habits are building, since health here is less an event than a running total. The hazards are fussiness and overdrive. You can tip into criticizing everyone's methods including your own, polishing details nobody needs, or treating yourself like equipment that exists to produce. Service, the house's older name, can slide into servitude if you say yes to every request just because you are competent. The peak of the transit is usually a moment of plain sight: you see exactly which parts of your routine serve you and which are just inherited clutter. Act on that sighting while the light is here. One habit genuinely adjusted, one recurring task automated or dropped, one boundary drawn around your working day, will outlast the month by a year. When the Sun moves on and other people become the story, you will be glad the machinery got its tune-up. This is the season that makes the rest of them run.

Other people carry the story while the Sun crosses your 7th house. For these few weeks each year, the light sits in the part of your chart that belongs to partners, and your life tilts toward the one-to-one: the spouse, the business partner, the close friend, the counterpart across the table, and sometimes the opponent. Where the opposite season is about your own initiative, this one runs on response. Plans go better with an ally now, decisions improve when talked through, and going it alone, which may be your usual comfort, costs more than it normally does. Relationships come into focus whether or not you aim them there. A partnership that is working tends to warm and deepen during the pass, often through some shared undertaking that shows you what the two of you are actually capable of. A partnership that has been coasting gets noticed, and the topics you have both been stepping around have a way of walking into the room. This is also a season when significant others need their share of the light. Letting a partner lead, shine, or decide, without keeping score, is precisely the skill the month develops. Negotiation runs through everything now: agreements, terms, the division of labor at home, who gives way and about what. You see yourself unusually clearly through other people's eyes during this transit, which is sometimes flattering and sometimes not, and both readings are worth having. The friction points are the classic ones. You can over-accommodate until you disappear, or swing the other way and turn every discussion into a contest. Open conflict, where it comes, tends to be clarifying rather than fatal if you stay on the subject and off the person. The peak of the pass is usually relational: a commitment made or renewed, a conflict faced, a partnership's real state said out loud. As the Sun moves on toward deeper waters, take stock of what the mirror showed you. The people closest to you have spent a month reflecting you with unusual accuracy. What you learned there is the season's yield, and it travels.

The Sun's yearly pass through your 8th house is one of the quieter transits, and one of the deeper ones. For a few weeks, your attention turns from the surface of life to its undercurrents: shared money, debts and taxes, inheritances and settlements, intimacy, and the parts of your own character you usually keep filed away. The season is not dark so much as honest. Things that were merely papered over become visible, and the light here works like an audit that includes the psyche along with the accounts. Joint resources make themselves felt first for many people. Whatever you hold together with someone else, a household budget, a loan, an estate, a business stake, tends to need attention now, and the underlying question is always the same: who owes what to whom, and is the arrangement still fair. Handled directly, these weeks are excellent for untangling exactly that. Intimacy deepens on the same principle. Closeness at this depth means being seen without the presentation, and the pass tends to create moments, wanted or not, where the presentation slips. What happens next depends on trust, and the month will tell you honestly how much of it there is. Your own interior gets louder too. Motives, jealousies, fears, and wants you do not usually consult all speak up, and old attachments you thought were finished may show a pulse. This is uncomfortable and useful in equal measure. The season's risks are brooding and control: circling a wound instead of dressing it, or gripping shared things tighter as a substitute for feeling safe. Its gift is release. Something often ends or is let go during this transit, a debt cleared, a resentment retired, an entanglement resolved, and the lightness afterward is real. The peak is often exactly that moment of release, and it rarely announces itself in advance. When the Sun climbs back toward open sky, you surface with less baggage than you carried in, which is the point. Once a year, this house asks what you are still holding that holds you back. Answering it even partially is enough.

Horizons widen when the Sun enters your 9th house. After the closed rooms of the previous season, these weeks throw the windows open: you want to go somewhere, learn something large, argue about ideas, and see your life from enough altitude that it makes sense as a whole. Restlessness with the familiar is the first sign of the pass. The commute, the usual opinions, the same four streets, all of it starts to feel small, and the appetite points at anything far away, foreign, or bigger than your daily frame. Travel suits the transit if you can get it, and even a short unfamiliar trip pays unusual dividends now. But distance is only one form of the theme. Study scratches the same itch: the course begun, the dense book actually read, the subject you circle back to every year finally given real hours. Teaching and publishing sit here too, so these are strong weeks for sharing what you know at scale, the talk, the essay, the class, anything that turns your experience into something others can use. Beliefs come up for review in this season. The convictions you run on, about how life works and what matters, get tested against new input, and some of them are due for revision. Held well, that is growth. Held poorly, it becomes the transit's classic vice: preaching, where you broadcast conclusions and quit hearing questions, certain in exact proportion to how little you have examined the idea lately. Watch also for the big plan drawn with no footings under it. Vision runs ahead of logistics all month, which is fine as long as you know which one you are doing. The peak of the pass is usually a sighting: from some vantage point, physical or mental, you see the shape of your life and where it is pointed, more clearly than the ground-level view ever shows. Bring one thing down the mountain. A question worth a year of study, a trip actually booked, a belief revised in writing. The Sun heads next toward the most public part of your chart, and the direction you sight now is the one you will be climbing in.

Your public standing warms while the Sun crosses the top of your chart. This pass through your 10th house is the high noon of your solar year: for a few weeks, the people who decide things, employers, clients, committees, audiences, can see you unusually well, and what you do in front of them counts for more than usual. Career matters concentrate now whether you invite them or not. Responsibility tends to find you, projects come to a head, and questions of direction, is this the work, is this the title, is this the reputation you want, press harder than they do the rest of the year. Ambition that has been idling wakes up. This is the natural season for the visible move: the application, the pitch to the person who can actually say yes, the finished work shipped under your own name, the moment you stop waiting to be noticed and step forward on purpose. Effort compounds while the light is here, because the same work done in an obscure month goes unseen and done now becomes part of your record. Authority is the other current. Dealings with bosses, institutions, and parents, especially any parent whose approval shaped your ambitions, tend to intensify, and how you handle power, yours and theirs, is on display. The exposure cuts both ways. Missteps show at the same magnification as achievements during this transit, and shortcuts have a way of being witnessed. Integrity is not decoration this month; it is structural. The other cost to watch is crowding, when the public claim on you grows until the private life that funds it starts running on fumes. The peak of the pass often arrives as a concrete event, a recognition, a promotion, a public result, or, just as usefully, as a clear reading of where you actually stand. Either way, aim the visibility. Attention gathered now attaches to whatever you are seen doing, so spend the weeks being seen doing the work you want more of. When the Sun tips past the summit, the glare softens, and what remains is whatever you built while everyone was watching.

Company arrives with the Sun's pass through your 11th house. For a few weeks each year, the light moves off your solo performance and onto the rooms you share: friends, teams, associations, communities, the whole web of people who are neither family nor audience but something more chosen. Invitations tend to multiply now, and accepting them pays. You are more visible in groups than usual, better at the introduction and the reunion, and the friendships that matter respond quickly to even modest attention: the call finally made, the visit finally scheduled. New alliances formed during this transit often prove durable, because they tend to form around something real, a project, a cause, an interest, rather than around convenience. Collective effort is the season's engine. Work that needs many hands, the team push, the community undertaking, the campaign, moves better now than in months when you would rather do everything yourself. Your role in the group is worth watching while the light is here. Some people discover they have quietly become a hub; others notice they have been orbiting rooms that no longer fit who they are. Both discoveries are useful. The house also holds the future, and mid-pass the long view usually opens: where is your life pointed, and are this year's efforts actually aimed at it. Hopes you shelved have a way of resurfacing during these weeks and asking whether they are still yours. Some are, and deserve a plan. Some belonged to an earlier version of you, and naming that releases real energy. The season's risks are dilution and drift, losing your own position inside the group's agenda, or collecting contacts while the actual friendships thin. Belonging is not the same as agreeing, and the month goes best when you bring a distinct self to the shared table. As the pass closes and the year turns toward its quiet final stretch, keep two things: one friendship deliberately reinforced, and one goal stated plainly enough that a friend could hold you to it. Ideally, tell that friend. The future arrives more reliably when someone else knows you are aiming at it.

The year exhales when the Sun slips into your 12th house. These are the closing weeks of your solar cycle, the last stretch before the Sun returns to your 1st house and starts you over, and they behave like the hour before dawn: quiet, inward, and not built for performance. Your energy for public life usually dips now. Crowds cost more, self-promotion feels hollow, and the appetite turns toward solitude, sleep, long walks, and time with your own thoughts. None of that is malfunction. The season is doing end-of-year work, and it does that work backstage. Endings come forward first. Projects, habits, and involvements that have run their course become obvious during this pass, and letting them close is easier than usual, almost a relief. Loose threads from the whole year, the unfinished task, the unsaid apology, the unfelt grief, tend to surface asking to be tied off, and each one handled now is one you do not drag into the new cycle. The inner life grows loud in the outer life's silence. Dreams pick up, memories visit, and feelings you outran in busier months catch up with you, which is their way of getting processed at last. Reflection, rest, and any practice that suits you, prayer, meditation, pages written for no reader, fits these weeks like a key. Compassion tends to deepen too, and quiet help given behind the scenes, with no credit attached, satisfies something the louder seasons never touch. The risks are the fog's two edges: forcing yourself to shine at full wattage and wondering why everything costs double, or hiding in escapes, screens, sleep, whatever your favorite exit is, until avoidance wears the costume of rest. The difference is how you feel afterward. Real rest restores; escape leaves the bill. There is no dramatic peak to this transit. Its high point is a subtle clearing, a morning when the year finally feels complete and something in you turns forward. Trust the timing. The Sun crosses into your 1st house soon after, energy returns with the light, and the cleaner you close this year, the brighter the next one opens.
